correctness.rationale: Prime powers have \(p\)-adic valuation exactly one below that required by \(p^a\). For \(pq\), the larger prime forces the unique pair \(2,3\). For squarefree \(pqr\), the largest prime cannot divide any factor from the two smaller blocks. For \(p^2q\), the necessary and sufficient local conditions are \(p\mid q^2-1\) and \(q\mid(p-1)(p^2+p+1)\). These yield the unique smaller-cofactor case \(18\) and, for \(q>p\), exactly \(q=p^2+p+1\) prime.

value.rationale: The residue-one condition is a natural divisibility question for the classical product \(\varphi(n)\sigma(n)\). The classification is unbounded, covers all factorization shapes through multiplicity three, and reveals an exact cyclotomic-prime mechanism in the first nontrivial repeated-prime layer.
